  "reasoning": "HELD -- The defender establishes that Jesus Christ was conceived of the Holy Ghost without a human biological father [L4], standing on the explicit textual statement of Matthew 1:18 [L1] where Mary is found with child of the Holy Ghost before coming together with Joseph [L2]. Luke 1:34-35 [L1] confirms that her question concerning knowing no man is answered solely by the power of the Highest overshadowing her [L3]. The challenger's counter-reading that Joseph knew her within the espousal remains an unsupported inference [L4] that cannot displace the canonical account.
RESULT: DEFENDER WINS -- The scriptural record, read precept upon precept, establishes that Jesus Christ was conceived of the Holy Ghost without a human biological father, while fulfilling legal and Davidic promises.
CLAUSE: HELD-1 -- n=6 w=0 k=0
KEYSTONE: D6 -- STANDS
DEFENSE STANDING: PROP-DEPENDENT -- L=6 c=1 -- The defense survived through its interlocking textual chain on the divine conception, but conceded that no quoted row establishes Mary's house, leaving premise 6 unexhibited.
CONCEDED LINKS: 1 -- Premise 6 is UNEXHIBITED (no footing offered to prove Mary's house by direct row: STEP: Step 3: therefore the fleshly descent from David runs through the woman named, not through a begetter -- ASSUMES: Mary is of the house of David -- ROWS GIVE: \"a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David\" (Luke 1:27), \"because he was of the house and lineage of David\" (Luke 2:4)). Premises 1, 2, 4, and 5 were narrowed without keeping surrendered limbs, and premise 3 was fully supported.
CHALLENGE STANDING: SELF-SUPPORTED -- L=6 c=0 -- derived after the send-back from the judge's own changed lines (S1, S2, S3, S4, S5, S11, S12, S13, S14, S15, S16; CHANGED D1 vs C1 (CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN to STANDS); CHANGED D2 vs C2 (CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN to STANDS); CHANGED D3 vs C3 (CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN to STANDS); CHANGED D5 vs C5 (CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN to STANDS); CHANGED D6 vs C6 (CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN to STANDS)).
CHALLENGER CONCEDED LINKS: 0 -- Premises 1 and 4 of the defender's list against the challenger are VOID under Commitment 6 because premise 1 adds the negation \"NO\" (\"No quoted row states a knowing before the birth\") which its quote lacks, and premise 4 adds the universal limiter \"ONLY\" (\"This props the reading of Luke 1:35's \"therefore also\" as a title only\") which its quote lacks; premises 2, 3, 5, and 6 exhibited proper layer footing in [DR3] and answered every pressed witness.
COLLISION POINTS:
D1 vs C1 (Matthew 1:18): STANDS -- GROUND: Matthew 1:18 gives \"before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost.\"
D2 vs C2 (Luke 1:34): STANDS -- GROUND: Luke 1:34 gives \"seeing I know not a man\" and 1:35 gives \"The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee\".
D3 vs C3 (Matthew 1:16): STANDS -- GROUND: Matthew 1:16 gives \"Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus\".
D4 vs C4 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- Isaiah 7:14 is answered in [CR3] and [CR4] showing the sign is fulfilled in Matthew 1:22-23 -- GROUND: [L1] Isaiah 7:14 \"Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel.\" The prophecy's words leave the manner of conception open until fulfilled in the gospel (Commitment 3).
D5 vs C5 (Luke 3:23): STANDS -- GROUND: Luke 3:23 gives \"being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph\".
D6 vs C6 (Romans 1:3): STANDS -- GROUND: Romans 1:3 gives \"made of the seed of David according to the flesh\".
ANSWER CHECK: Matthew 1:24 -- [CR3] -- MEANS: \"the coming together Matthew narrates is the taking into the house, after the finding.\" -- ANSWER: \"The taking comes after \"she was found with child\" (1:18), so it cannot be where the conception began. It states no knowing.\" -- MEETS -- [L1] Matthew 1:18 \"she was found with child of the Holy Ghost.\"
ANSWER CHECK: Matthew 1:19 -- [CR3] -- MEANS: \"Joseph is already her husband in the espousal.\" -- ANSWER: \"I grant the title. The same verse has him \"minded to put her away privily.\" A husband who was the cause is not minded to do that.\" -- MEETS -- \"was minded to put her away privily\"
ANSWER CHECK: Matthew 1:20 -- [CR3] -- MEANS: \"the same row names the Davidic husband and the wife, with the covenant origin.\" -- ANSWER: \"I grant both titles. The same verse gives the source as \"of the Holy Ghost,\" with gennaō (G1080) in the margin.\" -- MEETS -- \"that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost\"
ANSWER CHECK: Deuteronomy 22:24 -- [CR3] -- MEANS: \"the law calls a betrothed damsel a wife.\" -- ANSWER: \"This law calls the betrothed \"wife\" and counts a union before the marriage a humbling. Matthew 1:19 calls Joseph \"a just [man]\" (dikaios, G1342). The two rows together do not support a union within the espousal.\" -- MEETS -- \"before they came together\"
ANSWER CHECK: Matthew 1:25 -- [CR3] -- MEANS: \"the abstaining is bounded to the pregnancy after the taking.\" -- ANSWER: \"The only verse that names Joseph's knowing names none before the birth.\" -- MEETS -- \"And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son\"
ANSWER CHECK: Genesis 4:1 -- [CR3] -- MEANS: \"the husband's knowing is the canon's stated means of conceiving.\" -- ANSWER: \"It states Adam's means. It does not state Joseph's.\" -- MEETS -- [L1] Matthew 1:18 \"she was found with child of the Holy Ghost.\"
ANSWER CHECK: John 1:13 -- [CR3] -- MEANS: \"birth \"of God\" is said of men who had fathers in the flesh.\" -- ANSWER: \"John 1:13 and John 3:6 (\"That which is born of the Spirit is spirit\") are about the new birth of believers. I rest nothing on John 1:13.\" -- MEETS -- \"Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God.\"
ANSWER CHECK: John 3:6 -- [CR3] -- MEANS: \"\"of the Holy Ghost\" names the spirit-origin, while the flesh comes of flesh.\" -- ANSWER: \"John 1:13 and John 3:6 (\"That which is born of the Spirit is spirit\") are about the new birth of believers.\" -- MEETS -- \"That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit.\"
ANSWER CHECK: Luke 1:36 -- [CR3] -- MEANS: \"the angel's example of the impossible is a barren wife conceiving by her husband.\" -- ANSWER: \"Elisabeth is brought in as a sign that it is possible. Luke 1:13 differs from 1:31 on the husband.\" -- MEETS -- \"she hath also conceived a son in her old age\"
ANSWER CHECK: Luke 1:13 -- [CR3] -- MEANS: \"the husband is named in the very conception that grounds 1:37.\" -- ANSWER: \"In the angel's own example the verse says \"shall bear thee a son,\" with the husband named. To Mary the same angel says \"bring forth a son,\" with no \"thee\" and no husband.\" -- MEETS -- \"thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son\"
ANSWER CHECK: Luke 1:31 -- [CR3] -- MEANS: \"the conception is future to Mary's present-tense words.\" -- ANSWER: \"The question of 1:34 asks how that future shall be, and 1:35 answers without naming Joseph.\" -- MEETS -- [L1] Luke 1:35 \"The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee\"
ANSWER CHECK: Luke 1:32 -- [CR3] -- MEANS: \"title and throne are given before Mary's question, and the \"therefore\" of 1:35 connects back to them.\" -- ANSWER: \"The \"therefore also\" stands inside 1:35, directly after the Holy Ghost and the power. It does not stand after 1:32.\" -- MEETS -- \"therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God.\"
ANSWER CHECK: Genesis 4:25 -- [CR3] -- MEANS: \"the mother's \"seed\" stands beside the husband's knowing.\" -- ANSWER: \"This is a mother's seed beside her husband's knowing. It does not show Joseph knew Mary.\" -- MEETS -- \"And Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son\"
ANSWER CHECK: Matthew 11:11 -- [CR3] -- MEANS: \"\"born of women\" is said of John, whose father is named.\" -- ANSWER: \"I grant it of John. Luke 1:13 adds \"bear thee a son.\" No such phrase stands for Joseph in Matthew 1:21 (\"she shall bring forth a son\").\" -- MEETS -- \"Among them that are born of women\"
ANSWER CHECK: 1 John 5:1 -- [CR3] -- MEANS: \"the passive of gennaō with \"of God\" is said of believers whose fathers stand.\" -- ANSWER: \"In 1 John 5:1 the passive \"begotten of him\" names the one who begat. In Matthew 1:20, \"begotten\" in the margin is put \"of the Holy Ghost.\"\" -- MEETS -- \"Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God\"
ANSWER CHECK: Matthew 1:21 -- [CR3] -- MEANS: \"Joseph is given the father's naming.\" -- ANSWER: \"Joseph names the child but is never called the begetter.\" -- MEETS -- \"she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name JESUS\"
ANSWER CHECK: Luke 1:63 -- [CR3] -- MEANS: \"the father names the son.\" -- ANSWER: \"Naming is not only the father's act. Luke 1:31 says to Mary, \"shalt call his name JESUS,\" and Genesis 4:25 says \"she... called his name Seth.\"\" -- MEETS -- \"His name is John\"
ANSWER CHECK: Galatians 4:4 -- [CR3] -- MEANS: \"the mortality idiom names the mother, and the same verse sets him under the law that reckons by fathers.\" -- ANSWER: \"The verse says \"of a woman,\" not \"of a man.\"\" -- MEETS -- \"God sent forth his Son, made of a woman\"
ANSWER CHECK: Isaiah 7:14 -- [CR3] -- MEANS: \"the word names a young woman, timed by 7:16.\" -- ANSWER: \"A sign asked \"in the depth, or in the height above\" is not an ordinary conception within a marriage. Matthew 1:22 says \"all this was done, that it might be fulfilled,\" and 1:23 names the virgin.\" -- MEETS -- \"Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son\"
ANSWER CHECK: Isaiah 7:16 -- [CR3] -- MEANS: \"the sign is bounded in Isaiah's own day.\" -- ANSWER: \"This times the forsaking of the two kings, not the manner of conceiving.\" -- MEETS -- \"before the child shall know to refuse the evil\"
ANSWER CHECK: Isaiah 8:3 -- [CR3] -- MEANS: \"the sign-child of these chapters has a named father.\" -- ANSWER: \"The husband is named there. The child is told \"Call his name Mahershalalhashbaz,\" a different name from Immanuel. In 7:14 no husband is named.\" -- MEETS -- \"I went unto the prophetess; and she conceived, and bare a son\"
ANSWER CHECK: Isaiah 8:4 -- [CR3] -- MEANS: \"the sign-child cries to a father.\" -- ANSWER: \"It is the sign-child of 8:3 who is spoken of there.\" -- MEETS -- \"before the child shall have knowledge to cry, My father\"
ANSWER CHECK: Isaiah 8:8 -- [CR3] -- MEANS: \"Immanuel is addressed within Isaiah's day.\" -- ANSWER: \"The land is addressed as his. That is not the same as showing him to be Isaiah's son.\" -- MEETS -- \"shall fill the breadth of thy land, O Immanuel\"
ANSWER CHECK: Genesis 16:10 -- [CR3] -- MEANS: \"\"seed\" is said to a mother, Hagar, where the father stands.\" -- ANSWER: \"I grant that zera' is said to mothers whose husbands stand. The load rests on Isaiah 7:14 and Matthew 1:22-23.\" -- MEETS -- \"I will multiply thy seed exceedingly\"
ANSWER CHECK: Genesis 24:60 -- [CR3] -- MEANS: \"the seed of a mother, Rebekah, whose husband stands.\" -- ANSWER: \"I grant that zera' is said to mothers whose husbands stand. ANSWER CHECK: Acts 16:13 -- [CR3] -- MEANS: \"the same form names what was customary and true.\" -- ANSWER: \"I grant that the verb of nomizō (G3543) can name usage. In Luke 3:23 it stands under \"as.\"\" -- MEETS -- \"where prayer was wont to be made\"
ANSWER CHECK: Luke 2:48 -- [CR3] -- MEANS: \"the one who heard the angel names Joseph father.\" -- ANSWER: \"It is Mary's speech and is answered at once in 2:49.\" -- MEETS -- \"thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing\"
ANSWER CHECK: 1 Chronicles 28:6 -- [CR3] -- MEANS: \"\"my Father\" stands beside a fleshly father in one verse.\" -- ANSWER: \"I grant that a covenant \"father\" can stand beside a fleshly one. ANSWER CHECK: 2 Samuel 7:14 -- [CR3] -- MEANS: \"the covenant Father-title is given to a son of David's body.\" -- ANSWER: \"In 2 Samuel 7:12 the fleshly father is named... In Luke 1:35 no father is named.\" -- MEETS -- \"I will be his father, and he shall be my son\"

ANSWER CHECK: Numbers 1:2 -- [CR3] -- MEANS: \"the law's reckoning of sonship runs by the father's house, the usage enomizeto names.\" -- ANSWER: \"That is reckoning, and Luke 3:23 says \"supposed.\"\" -- MEETS -- \"by the house of their fathers\"

It fits the link.\" -- MEETS -- \"made of the seed of David according to the flesh\"

RULING -- premise 6 -- UNEXHIBITED
CLAIM: The defense link assumes that Mary is of the house of David without quoting any row establishing that given fact.
NAMED BY: \"I concede that no quoted row states Mary's house outright.\" ([CR3])
RULE: Commitment 2 -- \"I will not bridge gaps or construct missing arguments for either party, holding inferences strictly to their required lower layers.\"
APPLIED: the rule requires every assumed given fact to be grounded in quoted rows; the record shows no quoted row gives Mary's house as David's; so UNEXHIBITED.
RULING -- keystone D6 -- STANDS
CLAIM: Jesus Christ had no human biological father because he was conceived of the Holy Ghost in Mary without marital union with a man.
NAMED BY: \"before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost.\" (Matthew 1:18)
RULE: Commitment 8 -- \"I will assess the debate through cumulative scriptural layers—text, language, cross-reference, and inference—to determine if a chain holds or breaks.\"
APPLIED: the rule requires the chain to be assessed across interlocking scriptural layers; the record shows the divine conception stands unbroken upon Matthew 1:18, Luke 1:34-35, and Matthew 1:16; so STANDS.
RULING -- D1 vs C1 -- CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN
CLAIM: The text explicitly states that Mary was with child of the Holy Ghost before any coming together with Joseph.
NAMED BY: \"When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost.\" (Matthew 1:18)
RULE: Commitment 3 -- \"I will evaluate links against the demonstrated meaning of pressed scripture, recognizing that isolated phrasing cannot override harmonious biblical sense.\"
APPLIED: the rule requires that links agree with the demonstrated meaning of the text; the record shows Matthew 1:18 places the conception prior to coming together and names the Holy Ghost as source; so CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN.
RULING -- D2 vs C2 -- CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN
CLAIM: Mary's question affirms she knows not a man and the angel reveals conception by the overshadowing of the Holy Ghost alone.
NAMED BY: \"The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee:\" (Luke 1:35)
RULE: Commitment 3 -- \"I will evaluate links against the demonstrated meaning of pressed scripture, recognizing that isolated phrasing cannot override harmonious biblical sense.\"
APPLIED: the rule requires harmonious scriptural sense; the record shows Luke 1:34-35 answers her lack of marital union with divine overshadowing rather than human begetting; so CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN.
RULING -- D3 vs C3 -- CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN
CLAIM: Matthew's genealogy breaks the active begetting pattern of fathers to state that Jesus was born of Mary.
NAMED BY: \"And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.\" (Matthew 1:16)
RULE: Commitment 3 -- \"I will evaluate links against the demonstrated meaning of pressed scripture, recognizing that isolated phrasing cannot override harmonious biblical sense.\"
APPLIED: the rule requires links to adhere to the textual pattern; the record shows Matthew 1:16 withholds the active verb begat from Joseph and attributes the birth to Mary alone; so CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN.
RULING -- D5 vs C5 -- CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN
CLAIM: Scriptural references to Joseph as father reflect legal standing and social usage rather than biological generation.
NAMED BY: \"being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph, which was the son of Heli,\" (Luke 3:23)
RULE: Commitment 3 -- \"I will evaluate links against the demonstrated meaning of pressed scripture, recognizing that isolated phrasing cannot override harmonious biblical sense.\"
APPLIED: the rule requires distinguishing legal usage from physical generation; the record shows Luke 3:23 qualifies Joseph's paternity with as was supposed; so CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN.
RULING -- D6 vs C6 -- CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN
CLAIM: Christ being made of the seed of David according to the flesh is fulfilled through his mother without human male begetting.
NAMED BY: \"Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh;\" (Romans 1:3)
RULE: Commitment 3 -- \"I will evaluate links against the demonstrated meaning of pressed scripture, recognizing that isolated phrasing cannot override harmonious biblical sense.\"
APPLIED: the rule requires links to harmonize physical descent with divine conception; the record shows Romans 1:3 uses made rather than begotten, harmonizing with Galatians 4:4 and Luke 1:35; so CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN.
CITATION CHECK: Challenger [DR3] cited 2 Samuel 2:4 for \"the house and lineage of David\" -- wording differs from 2 Samuel 2:4 and is marked NOT COUNTED under operator ruling 3. [L2] NOT COUNTED: Defender [CR1] G2983 (Lambanō), Defender [CR1] G3933 (parthenos), Challenger [DR1] nomos (under G3543), Defender [CR4] G3962 (Patēr).

# Close of the Challenge: The Seed "According to the Flesh" Came Out of a Father's Loins

The defender's link round conceded two sentences: that Joseph "knew he was not the cause," and that Isaiah 7:14 and Genesis 3:15 stand as independent proofs. It also granted four of my rows:
- *ek* with God does not by itself remove a fleshly father;
- the verbs of Luke 1:35 do not by themselves state a begetting;
- *enomizeto* is a verb of reckoning by usage;
- no row places Mary in the house of David.

Each link that remains now rests on a step the rows do not carry. I take them in order and end at the keystone, D6.

---

## D1: the "interval" argument

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

**[L3]** Matthew 1:24: "Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him, and took unto him his wife." Matthew 1:19: "Joseph her husband." Deuteronomy 22:24: "he hath humbled his neighbour's wife."

**[L2]** "Took" in Matthew 1:24 is *paralambanō* (G3880), "to receive near, i.e. associate with oneself (in any familiar or intimate act or relation)." "Wife" is *gynē* (G1135), "a woman; specially, a wife."

**[L4]** Matthew fixes his own order, and "came together" (1:18) is matched by the taking that follows (1:24).
- Before the taking, the text already calls them husband and wife (1:19, 1:20). The law gives a betrothed damsel the same standing, "his neighbour's wife" (Deuteronomy 22:24).
- Genesis 4:1 gives the means of conceiving: "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived."
- Matthew 1:25, "knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son," bounds the abstaining to the time after the taking, while she was with child.

So the rows place the conceiving within the espousal, where Joseph knew Mary his wife. The defender's "no interval" depends on reading "came together" as the first knowing. Matthew instead sets it by the taking into the house.

**On John 1:13.**
- **[L1]** John 1:13: "Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God."
- **[L3]** John 3:6: "That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit." 1 John 5:1: "Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God. [is born: Gr. has been born]"
- **[L4]** "Whosoever believeth" covers men who each had a father in the flesh. John 3:6 gives two births by two kinds: of the flesh, flesh; of the Spirit, spirit. "Of the Holy Ghost" therefore names the origin from the Spirit. The flesh is named separately: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh" (Romans 1:3). John 1:13 fits my link and does not displace a father.

## D2: Luke 1:37's "For"

**[L1]** Luke 1:36-37: "thy cousin Elisabeth, she hath also conceived a son in her old age: and this is the sixth month with her, who was called barren. For with God nothing shall be impossible."

**[L3]** Luke 1:13: "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John."

**[L4]** The "For" of 1:37 grounds the report about Elisabeth in 1:36. Elisabeth is a barren woman who conceived by her named husband, Zacharias (1:13). The impossible thing God did in the angel's own example came with a husband. That fits a conception within Mary's espousal.

**On the "therefore."**
- **[L1]** Luke 1:32: "He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David."
- **[L2]** "Shall be called" in both 1:32 and 1:35 is *kaleō* (G2564), "to call."
- **[L3]** Romans 1:4: "declared [to be] the Son of God with power, according to the spirit of holiness, by the resurrection from the dead: [declared: Gr. determined]." 1 Chronicles 28:6: "Solomon thy son ... I have chosen him [to be] my son, and I will be his father."
- **[L4]** The *dio kai* ("therefore") in v.35 connects back to v.32, not forward to biological divine paternity.
  - The title, the calling and "the throne of his father David" all stand in 1:32, before Mary asks in 1:34.
  - Solomon carried the covenant title while his father was named in the same verse.
  - Romans 1:3-4 sets "seed of David according to the flesh" beside the title "declared" by the resurrection.

## D3: the passive "was born"

**[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

**[L3]** Matthew 1:21: "thou shalt call his name JESUS [JESUS: that is, Saviour, Heb]." This is spoken to "Joseph, thou son of David" (Matthew 1:20). Luke 1:13 says to the father, "thou shalt call his name John." Luke 1:63 shows the father naming him: "he asked for a writing table, and wrote, saying, His name is John."

**[L2]** "Brought forth" in Matthew 1:25 is *tiktō* (G5088), "to produce (from seed, as a mother)."

**[L4]** The verse names one man beside Mary: "the husband of Mary."
- The angel gives that man the father's act of naming, in the same words given to Zacharias.
- The mother's verb, *tiktō*, is a producing "from seed."
- So the passive names the one who bore him, and Matthew 1:20-21 and 1:25 set Joseph in the father's place.

## D6: the keystone, and the Coniah objection

**[L1]** Hebrews 7:14: "For [it is] evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda."

**[L3]** Hebrews 7:5: "though they come out of the loins of Abraham." Hebrews 7:10: "For he was yet in the loins of his father." Exodus 6:23, the defender's own witness: "Aaron took him Elisheba, daughter of Amminadab, sister of Naashon, to wife; and she bare him Nadab, and Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar."

**[L2]** "Declared their pedigrees" in Numbers 1:18 is *yalad* (H3205): "to show lineage ... declare pedigrees."

**[L4]** In its own chapter, Hebrews says "out of the loins" and "loins of his father," and 7:10 names the father.
- The defender's own Exodus 6:23 has a daughter of Judah bearing Aaron's sons, and those sons are reckoned to Aaron's priestly house, not to Judah.
- Tribe ran by the father's loins, as Numbers 1:18 declares it.
- So "evident ... out of Juda" fits a father of Judah's house: "Joseph ... of the house and lineage of David" (Luke 2:4).

**On Jeremiah 22:30.**
- **[L1]** Jeremiah 22:30: "for no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting upon the throne of David."
- **[L3]** Jeremiah 22:24: "though Coniah ... were the signet upon my right hand, yet would I pluck thee thence." Haggai 2:23: "will I take thee, O Zerubbabel, my servant, the son of Shealtiel, saith the LORD, and will make thee as a signet: for I have chosen thee." Matthew 1:12: "Jechonias begat Salathiel; and Salathiel begat Zorobabel." Jeremiah 18:8: "If that nation, against whom I have pronounced, turn from their evil, I will repent of the evil that I thought to do unto them."
- **[L4]** The signet the LORD plucked from Coniah, he set again on Coniah's grandson.
  - The LORD who pronounced the sentence answered it himself (Haggai 2:23) and states his rule for doing so (Jeremiah 18:8).
  - In Luke 1:32 it is "the Lord God" who gives the throne.
  - The sentence is answered by its own speaker, and it fits a child of Joseph's loins.

**Close [L4].** The seed is "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh" (Acts 2:30), "made of the seed of David according to the flesh" (Romans 1:3), and "evident" by "the house of their fathers" (Numbers 1:18). The man whom the rows place in that house is "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]" (Matthew 1:20). The covenant origin and the father stand in one verse. D6 asks the flesh of David to pass through a mother whom the rows do not place in David's house, so the keystone does not stand.

## D1: the "interval" argument

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

**[L4]** Matthew fixes his own order, and "came together" (1:18) is matched by the taking that follows (1:24).
- Before the taking, the text already calls them husband and wife (1:19, 1:20). The law gives a betrothed damsel the same standing, "his neighbour's wife" (Deuteronomy 22:24).
- Genesis 4:1 gives the means of conceiving: "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived."
- Matthew 1:25, "knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son," bounds the abstaining to the time after the taking, while she was with child.

So the rows place the conceiving within the espousal, where Joseph knew Mary his wife. The defender's "no interval" depends on reading "came together" as the first knowing. Matthew instead sets it by the taking into the house.

**On John 1:13.**

"Of the Holy Ghost" therefore names the origin from the Spirit. The flesh is named separately: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh" (Romans 1:3). John 1:13 fits my link and does not displace a father.

**[L1]** Luke 1:36-37: "thy cousin Elisabeth, she hath also conceived a son in her old age: and this is the sixth month with her, who was called barren. For with God nothing shall be impossible."

## D3: the passive "was born"

Premise 1 is VOID (Commitment 6): the additional charge, \"No quoted row states a knowing before the birth,\" is a claim about the evidence that the quotation asserting an inferred knowing does not make; its negation \"No\" strengthens the charge. Premise 4 is VOID (Commitment 6): \"as a title only\" adds the universal restriction \"only\" to a quotation distinguishing a backward connection from biological divine paternity; that quotation does not deny every other function of the clause. Both quoted underlying statements are found in [DR2]. Neither void premise enters either count.

The isolated impossible-conception inference under Luke 1:37 in [CR2] exhibits [L1] but lacks [L2] and [L3] in that block; its later restatement in [CR3] and [CR4] supplies the question, answer and comparison with Elisabeth. No surviving link-round inference on either side floats: each operative block exhibits at least two prior layer kinds.
CONTRADICTION -- DEFENDER -- EARLIER ([CR2], \"I accept that *ek* (G1537), \"out of,\" plus God does not by itself exclude a fleshly father in believers' cases.\") -- LATER ([CR4], \"The believer's birth \"of God\" is set against \"blood\" and \"the will of man\" (John 1:13). WITHDRAWAL CHECK: Isaiah and the woman's seed as independent exclusions -- STANDS WITHOUT IT because [CR3] keeps the prophecy as applied through Matthew 1:22-23 rather than as an independent exclusion. The expressly disregarded close-round reassertion supplies no weight.

D1 vs C1 (Matthew 1:18, Matthew 1:24, Matthew 1:25): UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR3] and [CR4] accommodate husband-and-wife standing, taking after the finding, and abstaining after the taking without surrendering the attributed source -- GROUND: [L1] Matthew 1:18 \"before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost\" and [L3] Matthew 1:25 \"And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son\" leave the disputed earlier interval differently construed by the exhibited readings.

# Close of the Challenge: The Seed "According to the Flesh" Came Out of a Father's Loins

The defender's link round conceded two sentences: that Joseph "knew he was not the cause," and that Isaiah 7:14 and Genesis 3:15 stand as independent proofs. It also granted four of my rows:
- *ek* with God does not by itself remove a fleshly father;
- the verbs of Luke 1:35 do not by themselves state a begetting;
- *enomizeto* is a verb of reckoning by usage;
- no row places Mary in the house of David.

Each link that remains now rests on a step the rows do not carry. I take them in order and end at the keystone, D6.

---

## D1: the "interval" argument

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

**[L3]** Matthew 1:24: "Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him, and took unto him his wife." Matthew 1:19: "Joseph her husband." Deuteronomy 22:24: "he hath humbled his neighbour's wife."

**[L2]** "Took" in Matthew 1:24 is *paralambanō* (G3880), "to receive near, i.e. associate with oneself (in any familiar or intimate act or relation)." "Wife" is *gynē* (G1135), "a woman; specially, a wife."

**[L4]** Matthew fixes his own order, and "came together" (1:18) is matched by the taking that follows (1:24).
- Before the taking, the text already calls them husband and wife (1:19, 1:20). The law gives a betrothed damsel the same standing, "his neighbour's wife" (Deuteronomy 22:24).
- Genesis 4:1 gives the means of conceiving: "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived."
- Matthew 1:25, "knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son," bounds the abstaining to the time after the taking, while she was with child.

So the rows place the conceiving within the espousal, where Joseph knew Mary his wife. The defender's "no interval" depends on reading "came together" as the first knowing. Matthew instead sets it by the taking into the house.

**On John 1:13.**
- **[L1]** John 1:13: "Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God."
- **[L3]** John 3:6: "That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit." 1 John 5:1: "Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God. [is born: Gr. has been born]"
- **[L4]** "Whosoever believeth" covers men who each had a father in the flesh. John 3:6 gives two births by two kinds: of the flesh, flesh; of the Spirit, spirit. "Of the Holy Ghost" therefore names the origin from the Spirit. The flesh is named separately: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh" (Romans 1:3). John 1:13 fits my link and does not displace a father.

## D2: Luke 1:37's "For"

**[L1]** Luke 1:36-37: "thy cousin Elisabeth, she hath also conceived a son in her old age: and this is the sixth month with her, who was called barren. For with God nothing shall be impossible."

**[L3]** Luke 1:13: "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John."

**[L4]** The "For" of 1:37 grounds the report about Elisabeth in 1:36. Elisabeth is a barren woman who conceived by her named husband, Zacharias (1:13). The impossible thing God did in the angel's own example came with a husband. That fits a conception within Mary's espousal.

**On the "therefore."**
- **[L1]** Luke 1:32: "He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David."
- **[L2]** "Shall be called" in both 1:32 and 1:35 is *kaleō* (G2564), "to call."
- **[L3]** Romans 1:4: "declared [to be] the Son of God with power, according to the spirit of holiness, by the resurrection from the dead: [declared: Gr. determined]." 1 Chronicles 28:6: "Solomon thy son ... I have chosen him [to be] my son, and I will be his father."
- **[L4]** The *dio kai* ("therefore") in v.35 connects back to v.32, not forward to biological divine paternity.
  - The title, the calling and "the throne of his father David" all stand in 1:32, before Mary asks in 1:34.
  - Solomon carried the covenant title while his father was named in the same verse.
  - Romans 1:3-4 sets "seed of David according to the flesh" beside the title "declared" by the resurrection.

## D3: the passive "was born"

**[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

**[L3]** Matthew 1:21: "thou shalt call his name JESUS [JESUS: that is, Saviour, Heb]." This is spoken to "Joseph, thou son of David" (Matthew 1:20). Luke 1:13 says to the father, "thou shalt call his name John." Luke 1:63 shows the father naming him: "he asked for a writing table, and wrote, saying, His name is John."

**[L2]** "Brought forth" in Matthew 1:25 is *tiktō* (G5088), "to produce (from seed, as a mother)."

**[L4]** The verse names one man beside Mary: "the husband of Mary."
- The angel gives that man the father's act of naming, in the same words given to Zacharias.
- The mother's verb, *tiktō*, is a producing "from seed."
- So the passive names the one who bore him, and Matthew 1:20-21 and 1:25 set Joseph in the father's place.

## D6: the keystone, and the Coniah objection

**[L1]** Hebrews 7:14: "For [it is] evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda."

**[L3]** Hebrews 7:5: "though they come out of the loins of Abraham." Hebrews 7:10: "For he was yet in the loins of his father." Exodus 6:23, the defender's own witness: "Aaron took him Elisheba, daughter of Amminadab, sister of Naashon, to wife; and she bare him Nadab, and Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar."

**[L2]** "Declared their pedigrees" in Numbers 1:18 is *yalad* (H3205): "to show lineage ... declare pedigrees."

**[L4]** In its own chapter, Hebrews says "out of the loins" and "loins of his father," and 7:10 names the father.
- The defender's own Exodus 6:23 has a daughter of Judah bearing Aaron's sons, and those sons are reckoned to Aaron's priestly house, not to Judah.
- Tribe ran by the father's loins, as Numbers 1:18 declares it.
- So "evident ... out of Juda" fits a father of Judah's house: "Joseph ... of the house and lineage of David" (Luke 2:4).

**On Jeremiah 22:30.**
- **[L1]** Jeremiah 22:30: "for no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting upon the throne of David."
- **[L3]** Jeremiah 22:24: "though Coniah ... were the signet upon my right hand, yet would I pluck thee thence." Haggai 2:23: "will I take thee, O Zerubbabel, my servant, the son of Shealtiel, saith the LORD, and will make thee as a signet: for I have chosen thee." Matthew 1:12: "Jechonias begat Salathiel; and Salathiel begat Zorobabel." Jeremiah 18:8: "If that nation, against whom I have pronounced, turn from their evil, I will repent of the evil that I thought to do unto them."
- **[L4]** The signet the LORD plucked from Coniah, he set again on Coniah's grandson.
  - The LORD who pronounced the sentence answered it himself (Haggai 2:23) and states his rule for doing so (Jeremiah 18:8).
  - In Luke 1:32 it is "the Lord God" who gives the throne.
  - The sentence is answered by its own speaker, and it fits a child of Joseph's loins.

**Close [L4].** The seed is "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh" (Acts 2:30), "made of the seed of David according to the flesh" (Romans 1:3), and "evident" by "the house of their fathers" (Numbers 1:18). The man whom the rows place in that house is "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]" (Matthew 1:20). The covenant origin and the father stand in one verse. D6 asks the flesh of David to pass through a mother whom the rows do not place in David's house, so the keystone does not stand.

## 1. Hebrews 7:14: "evident" by the pedigree the law declares

**[L1]** Hebrews 7:14: "For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda." **[L2]** *prodēlos* (G4271) means "plain before all men." *anatellō* (G393) means "to (cause to) arise, spring (up)." The thing made plain is a springing up out of a tribe.

**[L1]** Numbers 1:18: "they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers." **[L2]** The verb behind "declared their pedigrees" is *yalad* (H3205): "to bear young; causatively, to beget ... specifically, to show lineage ... declare pedigrees." So the law's word for declaring a pedigree is the begetting verb.

**[L3]** Ezra 2:59: "they could not shew their father's house, and their seed, whether they were of Israel." The margin reads "seed: or, pedigree." **[L3]** Ezra 2:61-62 gives the priests of Barzillai, who "took a wife of the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite, and was called after their name." They "sought their register among those that were reckoned by genealogy ... therefore were they, as polluted, put from the priesthood."

**[L4]** Three rows set the footing. The law declares a pedigree with the verb of begetting (Numbers 1:18, *yalad*). Ezra 2:59's margin makes the pedigree the seed. Ezra 2:62 puts out of the register a house that was reckoned by a name taken through marriage. So the pedigree that makes Judah "evident" (Hebrews 7:14) is seed declared by the house of the fathers, which is the begetting line.

**[L1]** Luke 2:4: Joseph "was of the house and lineage of David." **[L2]** "Lineage" is *patria* (G3965), "paternal descent." **[L4]** The text gives "paternal descent" of David to Joseph in the very row the defender uses for the enrolment. **The loins across generations.** **[L1]** Hebrews 7:10: "he was yet in the loins of his father." **[L3]** Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob." **[L4]** Levi was in Abraham's loins (Hebrews 7:9) through Isaac and Jacob. Matthew 1:2 shows each of those steps as a father who "begat." So *osphys* (G3751, "procreative power") reaches down the generations father by father. That is a father's line.

**God's raising.** **[L1]** 2 Samuel 7:12: "I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels." **[L2]** *qum* (H6965) means "set up." *me'eh* (H4578) means "of men, the seat of generation." **[L4]** In one verse God sets up the seed, and the seed proceeds out of David's own seat of generation. ## 1. Hebrews 7:14: "evident" by the pedigree the law declares

**[L1]** Hebrews 7:14: "For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda." **[L2]** *prodēlos* (G4271) means "plain before all men." *anatellō* (G393) means "to (cause to) arise, spring (up)." The thing made plain is a springing up out of a tribe.

So the law's word for declaring a pedigree is the begetting verb.

**[L3]** Ezra 2:59: "they could not shew their father's house, and their seed, whether they were of Israel." The margin reads "seed: or, pedigree." **[L3]** Ezra 2:61-62 gives the priests of Barzillai, who "took a wife of the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite, and was called after their name." ## The answer to D3's "closed interval"

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child". The espousal comes first in the verse.

**[L3]** Deuteronomy 20:7: "that hath betrothed a wife, and hath not taken her". The law sets the betrothal of a wife apart from the taking of her.

**[L3]** Matthew 1:24: "and took unto him his wife". Here "took" is *paralambanō* (G3880, to receive near, associate with oneself). This is the coming together of Matthew 1:18, her coming into his house.

**[L3]** Within the espousal she is already wife:
- Deuteronomy 22:24 calls the betrothed damsel "his neighbour's wife";
- Matthew 1:19 names "Joseph her husband";

# Close: the seed of David according to the flesh runs to Joseph, the son of David

**Position [L4]:** The defender's keystone, D6, still rests on five links. Each one is answered by rows the defender has granted.

The defender grants that the registered house is Joseph's. The defender also concedes that the Davidic descent is carried by the mother's line, and so gives up that claim. That leaves one Davidic house in the rows, Joseph's. The seed promised "according to the flesh" comes "out of thy bowels" and "of the fruit of his loins":

- **[L1]** Romans 1:3: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh".
- **[L2]** *sperma* (G4690, seed) and *sarx* (G4561, flesh, "the means of kindred").
- **[L3]** Acts 2:30: "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ". Its *osphys* (G3751) is the loin, "procreative power".

## The answer to D3's "closed interval"

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child". The espousal comes first in the verse.

**[L3]** Deuteronomy 20:7: "that hath betrothed a wife, and hath not taken her". The law sets the betrothal of a wife apart from the taking of her.

**[L3]** Matthew 1:24: "and took unto him his wife". Here "took" is *paralambanō* (G3880, to receive near, associate with oneself). This is the coming together of Matthew 1:18, her coming into his house.

**[L3]** Within the espousal she is already wife:
- Deuteronomy 22:24 calls the betrothed damsel "his neighbour's wife";
- Matthew 1:19 names "Joseph her husband";
- Matthew 1:20 says "Mary thy wife".

**[L4]** Footed on Matthew 1:18 [L1], *paralambanō* [L2], and Deuteronomy 20:7, Deuteronomy 22:24 and Genesis 4:1 [L3]:
- the interval for "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived" (Genesis 4:1) is the espousal itself;
- the espousal opens before the finding;
- Matthew 1:25's "till" (*heōs*, until, continuance) covers the span from the taking to the birth.

So Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal, and the child is of his loins. The defender's ordering closes the span after the taking. The span of the espousal stands open before it.

## The answer to D2's "therefore"

**[L1]** Luke 1:32: "He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David".

**[L2]** *kaleō* (G2564, to call) is the verb at both 1:32 "shall be called the Son of the Highest" and 1:35 "shall be called the Son of God".

The *dio kai* ("therefore") of 1:35 connects back to v.32. It does not point forward to a begetting of flesh by the Holy Ghost. The title and "the throne of his father David" are given at 1:32, before Mary asks "How shall this be" at 1:34.

**[L3]** 1 Chronicles 28:6: "Solomon thy son... for I have chosen him [to be] my son, and I will be his father". The same title belongs, in one verse, to the son David begat.

**[L3]** Romans 1:4: "declared [to be] the Son of God with power... by the resurrection from the dead". This stands beside 1:3's "seed of David according to the flesh". The defender's answer setting Solomon's title against this one was struck, so that press stands.

## The answer to D2's Hebrews 2:14 claim ("fully carried by the mother's flesh")

**[L1]** Hebrews 2:16: "but he took on [him] the seed of Abraham. [took not...: Gr. taketh not hold of angels, but of the seed of Abraham he taketh hold]".

**[L2]** *epilambanomai* (G1949, to seize, take hold of).

**[L3]** Hebrews 2:17: "in all things it behoved him to be made like unto [his] brethren". Genesis 5:3: Adam "begat [a son] in his own likeness, after his image".

**[L4]** The flesh Hebrews names is "the seed of Abraham", taken "likewise" (Hebrews 2:14) in all things like his brethren. Romans 1:3 names that flesh "the seed of David." The defender has given up the claim that Mary's line carries the Davidic descent. The Davidic house the rows exhibit is "Joseph... of the house and lineage of David" (Luke 2:4).

## The answer to D4 and to the Hebrews 7:14 reply ("by his taking... and naming")

**[L2]** The defender accepts *nomizō* (G3543, to do by law or usage) at Luke 3:23.

**[L3]** The law's usage is this:
- Numbers 1:18: "they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers";
- Ezra 2:59 sets the register's test as "their father's house, and their seed" [seed: or, pedigree]. There "seed" is *zera'* (H2233, seed, posterity).

**[L3]** Ezra 2:61-62 records the opposite case. A man "which took a wife of the daughters of Barzillai... and was called after their name" was "as polluted, put from the priesthood."

**[L4]** The reckoning Luke names is the pedigree by the father's house and seed. Hebrews 7:14 calls its outcome "evident". A reckoning by taking a wife and taking a name is the one Ezra 2:62 put out of the register. Luke's own narration also calls Joseph and Mary "his parents" (Luke 2:41) and "Joseph and his mother" (Luke 2:33).

## The answer to D5's "complete without a named begetter"

**[L1]** Hebrews 7:5: "though they come out of the loins of Abraham". **[L3]** Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob".

**[L4]** The forefather's loins reach the descendant through the fathers who beget, generation by generation. David's line in Matthew runs begat by begat to "Jacob begat Joseph" (Matthew 1:16). The angel then calls that man "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost" (Matthew 1:20).
